lines.text: Why can I see my breath when it's cold?
Because you're breathing. Congrats.
Nah. Cold air unlocks my dragon powers.
Your lungs are a very damp place.
Every breath out is warm and full of invisible water vapor.
Outside, it hits the cold air and loses heat fast.
Once it cools to its dew point, some vapor turns into liquid.
Thousands of tiny water droplets. That's what you see.
Wait. So I'm breathing out... a cloud?
A very small, very temporary cloud. Yes.
Excuse me. My cloud is majestic.
Real clouds and fog form the exact same way.
So I'm basically weather. Call me the forecast.
Partly cloudy. Mostly annoying.
A second later, the droplets evaporate again. Poof.
So it has to be below freezing?
Nope. On a humid morning, you can see it in the forties.
So on a dry day... my dragon is cancelled.
Your dragon was never real. And now you know.
Brr. It's freezing out here. Quick question...
